name: Game-Theoretic Local Masking
description: Replaces the direct inequality condition (`c_u != c_v`) with the evaluation of a combinatorial game (Wythoff's game) played on piles of size `c_u` and `c_v`. Since the domain is strictly `{1, 2}`, a second-player win precisely isolates the pairs `(1, 2)` and `(2, 1)`. This forces the model to correctly evaluate the game theory constraint to discover the inequality, and then recognize the resulting global structure as bipartite coloring, defeating models that rely on simple algebraic pattern matching.
